channel.title: Hesed Words — Reflections
channel.description: Devotional reflections by Norm Reed. Scripture, justice, and the love that holds. Written for the road.

item.title: How Precious
item.description: Precious is a valuer's word, the word for precious stones, and Psalm 36:7 uses it of God's hesed. Gollum's ring let itself be held. Hesed does not; you take refuge under it.

item.title: An Invitation to Strike
item.description: David asks to be heard, and in the same prayer asks to be struck, and calls the striking hesed. A God who only ever agreed with me would not be listening to me.

item.title: Maturity?
item.description: Paul offers the Corinthians a secret wisdom for the mature, and the secret turns out to be Jesus on a cross, in plain sight. A few lines later he tells them they are still babies.

item.title: Then We Stopped
item.description: At Caesarea nobody was persuaded and nobody won. They fell quiet, said let the will of the Lord be done, and carried the luggage. Six months after a cardiac arrest, I have stopped arguing too.

item.title: I Arrived Late
item.description: Lydda, Joppa and Caesarea are one story with a direction, and every stage of it is somebody else's errand. Peter got there late, after it had already happened. Perhaps I am still late.

item.title: According to Your Steadfast Love
item.description: Psalm 119 is the law psalm, but another word runs through it only seven times: hesed. It turns up when he prays. And the longest psalm about God's word ends with a sheep that has wandered off, asking the shepherd to come and find him.

item.title: You Have Judged Rightly
item.description: Simon answers the parable correctly and does not notice whose case he has just decided. She never says a word, and Jesus calls it faith.

item.title: The Man Who Fears the Lord
item.description: Two psalms built to the same alphabet, one about God and one about a man, using the same words of both. Ask most people what it means to fear God and you get a list of things a person does not do. Psalm 112 answers with a list of things he does.

item.title: Who Knows
item.description: Jonah's sermon is five words long and the mercy is left out. A pagan king had to guess at the thing the preacher could have told him — and his guess was right. Being right is not the same as passing it on.

item.title: Asking for Bread
item.description: They crossed a lake to find him, and he answered a question they had not asked. He does not tell them to stop seeking — he tells them what is underneath it. I sit in prayer meetings, and what I hear, most of the time, is people asking for bread. So do I.

item.title: You Should!
item.description: A friend who pounces on one phrase, a phone call to the UK, and a courtyard where nobody was given a verdict. He gave her a road; they had given her a label.

item.title: Somebody Else Was Awake
item.description: The watchman with nothing to guard. He never finds out that somebody else was awake that night, listening for exactly the sound he was making. We are told. He is not.

item.title: What Do You Want Me to Do for You
item.description: How much of Mark 8 to 10 is Jesus asking things. Ask me what Jesus taught and I can tell you; ask me what he asked people and I would have to stop and think.

item.title: The Asking
item.description: Psalm 98 is nine verses and most of them are instructions to make noise. Verse 3 is the only place where God does something, and it is quiet. You have delegated the responsibility, but not the provision to be merciful.

item.title: Still Talking
item.description: Psalm 94 never gets fixed. The wicked are still boasting in the last line, and nobody stood up when he asked. What holds him is not rescue.
